title: Observability Stack
description: The stack watching itself: what Alloy is collecting, whether it reaches Prometheus and Loki, and how close the two stores are to their retention limits.

panels.title: Targets Down
panels.description: A discovered target Alloy cannot reach. Check the two network policies first: the workload's ingress and Alloy's egress.

panels.title: Samples In
panels.description: Samples per second landing in Prometheus.

panels.title: Active Series
panels.description: Cardinality. This is what makes Prometheus run out of memory, not the sample rate.

panels.title: TSDB Size
panels.description: Retention is 15 days or 4GB, whichever comes first. Above ~3.5GB the window starts shrinking below 15 days.

panels.title: Remote Write Failures (1h)
panels.description: Samples Alloy could not hand to Prometheus. Sustained failures mean gaps in every graph.

panels.title: Targets by Job
panels.description: A job dropping to zero means the whole component stopped being discovered.

panels.title: Samples Sent to Prometheus
panels.description: Alloy scrapes and forwards; Prometheus only stores. Failures here become gaps in every metric panel in this folder.

panels.title: Remote Write Backlog
panels.description: A growing backlog means Prometheus is not keeping up with what Alloy collects.

panels.title: Scrape Duration by Job
panels.description: Approaching the scrape interval means the target is too slow to scrape reliably.

panels.title: Alloy Resource Usage
panels.description: Alloy is clustered and splits targets between replicas. The memory limit is 512Mi.

panels.title: Active Series
panels.description: Watch the trend, not the number. Steady growth without new workloads means something is emitting high cardinality labels.

panels.title: Storage Used
panels.description: Retention stops at 4GB or 15 days. The PVC is 10Gi, so the size cap binds first.

panels.title: Rejected Samples
panels.description: Prometheus accepts a 10 minute out-of-order window (out_of_order_time_window). Duplicates usually mean two Alloy replicas scraping the same target.

panels.title: Chunk Flushing
panels.description: Loki runs SingleBinary on a filesystem store; flushed chunks land on the 10Gi PVC.

panels.title: Request Latency by Route
panels.description: Push is Alloy writing; query_range is Grafana reading.

panels.title: Grafana Query Latency by Datasource
panels.description: How long Grafana waits on Prometheus and Loki. Slow queries here are usually a dashboard asking for too long a range, not a sick store.

panels.title: Grafana HTTP Responses
panels.description: Grafana's own HTTP traffic, through the gateway.

panels.title: Stack Memory Usage
panels.description: All four components share the monitoring namespace. Every one of them has a memory limit set in infrastructure/base.
